newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banks to pool 50 bln baht to rescue stocks.
newsitem.headline: Thai banks to pool 50 bln baht to rescue stocks.

text.p: Thai commercial banks have volunteered to pool up to 50 billion baht to shore up the nation's battered stock market while the government will slash the 1997/98 budget, newspapers on Sunday quoted Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan as saying.
The stock rescue fund proposal was initiated by commercial banks, the papers quoted Amnuay as announcing after chairing an unscheduled meeting of finance and economic officials on Saturday.
Amnuay said he was also confident that Thai commercial banks would cut lending rates by another one to two percentage points later this year to give cash-strapped businesses access to cheaper funds.

The Thai cabinet is expected to consider next Wednesday the finance minister's budget cut which would reduce planned 1997/1998 (October/September) government expenditure by about 26 billion baht ($1 billion) to 982 billion baht.
Amnuay was quoted as saying that the cut would help sustain Thailand's policy of adopting balanced, deficit-free budgets.
The minister had earlier trimmed the 1996/1997 budget by 59 billion baht in line with a sharply slowing Thai economy, which has caused the government to miss its tax revenue target this year.

Thai stocks plunged to near eight-year lows over the past week after foreign currency speculators attacked the baht on rumours that Thailand may devalue its currency and talk of conflicts within the government over economic policies.
The baht rallied strongly on Thursday and Friday after the Bank of Thailand, with help from Singapore and other regional central banks, spent billions of dollars to defend the currency.
Amnuay and Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh have repeatedly denied the rumours.
